common_name: Golden Dragon Impatiens / Ceylon Jewelweed / Creeping Balsam

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or nursery starts after all frost danger has passed; this species is critically rare in its native Sri Lankan habitat and is propagated almost exclusively from stem cuttings rather than seed in cultivation.

directions: Grow in a humus-rich, moist but well-draining mix in a hanging basket or as a groundcover in deep to partial shade, since the fleshy red trailing stems root readily where they touch soil. Allow the surface to dry slightly between waterings rather than keeping the semi-succulent stems constantly saturated, which can lead to rot. The hooded, bright golden-yellow flowers appear along the trailing stems from summer into autumn against small, dark green, red-backed leaves. Protect from temperatures below 50°F, as this tender species has no frost tolerance and is typically overwintered indoors as a houseplant outside of zones 10-11.

common_name: Fusion Glow Impatiens (Exotic New Guinea Impatiens Hybrid)

planting.note: Set out transplants after the last frost into partial shade to partial sun in fertile, well-drained soil; Fusion is a vegetatively propagated exotic impatiens bred for smaller, more profuse blooms and a looser, wider-spreading habit than standard New Guinea impatiens.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in partial shade to partial sun, and feed regularly to sustain its nonstop flowering habit through the season. Fusion Glow is a Ball-bred exotic impatiens hybrid that carries smaller, more numerous flowers than typical New Guinea impatiens, in a warm apricot-orange blend brushed with buttery yellow, on a mounding, slightly trailing plant well suited to mixed containers and hanging baskets. It tolerates more sun and heat than traditional Impatiens walleriana while still preferring some afternoon shade in hot climates, and its self-cleaning flowers need no deadheading. Consistent moisture keeps the compact mounds full; allowing the plant to dry out repeatedly will thin the bloom count.

common_name: SunPatiens Spreading Shell Pink Impatiens (Mounding Sun-Tolerant New Guinea Impatiens)
scientific_name: Impatiens x hybrida 'SunPatiens Spreading Shell Pink'

planting.note: Set out transplants after all frost danger has passed into full sun to partial shade in fertile, well-drained soil; SunPatiens Spreading is the mid-size, mounding tier of the SunPatiens line, sized between the tidy Compact series and the tall, upright Vigorous series.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in fertile, well-drained soil, feeding regularly to support the broad, mounding growth this tier of the SunPatiens line is bred for. SunPatiens Spreading Shell Pink forms a wide, low mound 24 to 30 inches tall and wide, covered in soft, pale pink flowers from spring through frost, filling more horizontal space than the upright Vigorous series while growing taller and fuller than the Compact series. Like the rest of the SunPatiens breeding line, it carries strong resistance to impatiens downy mildew and tolerates considerably more sun and heat than traditional shade impatiens. Its broad habit makes it well suited to large hanging baskets, ground-level mass plantings, and filling wide garden beds without staking.
sources: Mississippi State University Extension — Truck Crops Trial Garden

common_name: Fiesta Salsa Double Impatiens (Fully Double Rose-Form Impatiens)

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated transplants after the last frost into shade to partial shade in fertile, well-drained soil; Fiesta is a fully double-flowered impatiens series bred to resemble miniature roses on a classic mounded walleriana habit.

directions: Plant in fertile, evenly moist, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade, and water often since the fully double blooms and lush foliage wilt quickly in dry conditions. Fiesta Salsa produces densely packed, fully double, rose-red flowers that resemble miniature roses rather than the flat, five-petaled form of standard impatiens, held above compact, well-branched mounds. Because it is vegetatively propagated rather than seed-grown, it comes true to the double flower form with excellent uniformity across a planting, unlike some older double-impatiens seed strains that segregate to singles. Feed lightly on a regular schedule and pinch any leggy stems in midsummer to keep the mounded habit tidy through the season.
sources: Ball FloraPlant — Fiesta Impatiens series notes
